study type: secondary analysis of a prospective cohort study
outcome: laboratory evidence of hemorrhage (decrease in hemoglobin ≥ 4 mg/dL)
clinical evidence of hemorrhage (atony, transfusion, coagulopathy, hysterectomy, laparotomy, or intensive care unit admission)
cohort: 54,597 women delivering by cesarean or vaginal birth after cesarean.
finding: Thrombocytopenia (platelets <150,000/mL) was associated with both laboratory and clinical evidence of postpartum hemorrhage, with the risk increasing with the severity of thrombocytopenia.
